0.0.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

0.2.n: This is her family name, placed before her given name in Japanese.

0.4.n: A polite sentence ending; the speaker leaves out the understood subject 私, meaning I.

1.0.n: Refers to the current video or presentation.

1.1.n: Marks 今回 as the topic, setting the context for this presentation.

1.2.n: Combines with 均 to form 100均, the common shorthand for 100-yen shops.

1.3.n: Short for 均一, meaning uniform; together with 100, it refers to 100-yen shops.

1.4.n: Here マニア describes someone very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about 100-yen shops, not someone dangerous.

1.5.n: Marks マニア as the person doing the choosing in 選ぶ.

1.6.n: The plain form directly describes 購入品: purchases that the enthusiast chooses.

1.8.n: This is the name of a Japanese discount-store chain.

1.9.n: Connects ダイソー to 購入品, identifying the store the purchases came from.

1.10.n: Combines 購入, buying, with 品, goods, to refer to what she bought.

1.11.n: Marks 購入品 as what she will introduce.

1.12.n: 紹介する becomes 紹介して + いきます, politely presenting the introductions as something she will proceed with.

2.0.n: Sets the scope of her selection to this particular video.

2.1.n: Marks 今回 as the topic of the sentence.

2.2.n: The prefix お makes 掃除 sound softer and more polite.

2.3.n: The English loanword グッズ combines with お掃除 to describe cleaning products or tools.

2.4.n: Lists examples rather than giving a complete list.

2.5.n: Describes the purpose of the following グッズ: putting things away or organizing them.

2.6.n: Together with 収納, this refers to organizers and other storage products.

2.7.n: Shows that cleaning and storage products are examples, not the entire selection.

2.9.n: Names the everyday setting in which these items are useful.

2.10.n: Marks 日常 as the setting where the items can be used.

2.11.n: Describes usefulness and combines with に to modify how the items can be used.

2.12.n: Turns 便利 into a description of how something is used.

2.13.n: The can-do form of 使う directly describes アイテム.

2.14.n: An English loanword referring here to the products she selected.

2.15.n: Part of を中心に, which identifies the main focus of her selection.

2.16.n: Literally center; here it identifies the products she concentrated on selecting.

2.17.n: Completes を中心に, meaning focusing mainly on what comes before it.

2.18.n: 選んで is the て-form of 選ぶ; adding みました politely says she tried making this selection.

3.0.n: Combines with に to emphasize hands-on use rather than just showing the products.

3.1.n: Turns 実際 into a description of how she will use the products.

3.2.n: The shortened connecting form of 使う attaches to ながら.

3.3.n: Shows that the same person uses the products and introduces them at the same time.

3.4.n: 紹介して + いく presents the introductions as progressing from this point onward.

3.5.n: Gives her demonstrations as the reason for the request that follows.

3.7.n: Adds warm encouragement to the request, rather than making it compulsory.

3.8.n: The prefix お adds a polite, friendly tone to 買い物.

3.9.n: Follows お買い物 to specify the time before shopping.

3.10.n: Links お買い物前 to 参考, describing guidance intended for before shopping.

3.11.n: Refers to information viewers can use to help decide what to buy.

3.12.n: In 参考にする, に marks the role something is given: a reference or guide.

3.13.n: する becomes して + ください to make a polite request; 参考にする means to use something as a reference.

0.tip: Japanese introductions usually put the family name first and omit I.

1.lit: This time, a 100-yen-shop enthusiast chooses Daiso purchases; I will proceed to introduce them.
1.tip: マニアが選ぶ describes the purchases directly: items an enthusiast chooses.

2.lit: This time, cleaning goods, storage goods, and such: focusing on items usable conveniently in daily life, I tried selecting.
2.tip: を中心に means focusing mainly on, so everyday usefulness is her main selection criterion.

3.lit: Actually using while introducing will proceed, so by all means make this a reference before shopping, please.
3.tip: Attach ながら to a verb’s connecting form to say you do something while doing another action.
